$frozen: FROZEN. Generated once by backend/tools/generate_sync_vectors.py and asserted byte-for-byte by both backend/tests/sync/ and app/test/sync/. Never regenerated by a test or by CI: regenerating is a protocol change.
$note: Ops here are payload-level, paired with the header author the reducer's guards check against. Envelope framing is envelope_v1_vectors.json's job. 'expected_entities' lists the live fields of every live entity after applying the ops in order; an entity with no live field is absent from the map.
$case_schema: Three optional per-case keys, all added by #550 and honoured by every runner. 'permute': apply the ops in every order and assert the reduced state is identical across all of them — a values-only pairwise case cannot catch an associativity failure. 'expected_clocks': the stored per-field HLC as {collection: {entity_id: {field: [wall_ms, counter, member_hex]}}}, asserted against `field_clocks` regardless of tombstone visibility, because a non-LWW strategy joins the clock independently of the value and nothing else observes that. 'strategy_overrides': {preference_key: strategy_name} for keys with no production strategy — today only 'set_merge', which is provisioned but unregistered. #555 adds a per-*op* key: 'op_class', present only when it is not 1, which the runner passes to the class-4 shape guard before the payload reaches the reducer.

cases.name: single_write
cases.note: The base case: one field, one HLC, one live entity.

cases.name: same_field_newer_hlc_wins
cases.note: Applied in HLC order.

cases.name: same_field_older_hlc_loses_out_of_order
cases.note: Same two ops, reversed arrival. Reduction is order-independent.

cases.name: field_grain_concurrent_different_fields_both_survive
cases.note: AC 5: concurrent edits to different fields of one row both survive.

cases.name: equal_hlc_is_idempotent
cases.note: A pulled echo of one's own op re-applies to the same state.

cases.name: member_id_breaks_the_tie
cases.note: Equal wall_ms and counter: the member id decides, by lexicographic compare of the 32-hex form.

cases.name: tombstone_absorbs_older_write
cases.note: A field write older than the tombstone stays hidden.

cases.name: tombstone_resurrection_by_newer_write
cases.note: The mirror case: a field write newer than the tombstone applies and revives the entity, with only that field live.

cases.name: per_field_hlc_from_another_member_in_the_past_applies
cases.note: F15 scoping, as ruled for this slice: the future-clock and hlc-member-equals-author guards are scoped to the op-level HLC *only*. A per-field HLC naming a different member at an older wall_ms is legal — that is exactly what a compaction op (#555) will carry — so it applies rather than quarantining.

cases.name: per_field_hlc_loses_to_a_newer_stored_clock
cases.note: The per-field exemption is from the *guards*, not from LWW: a re-asserted older clock still loses to a newer stored one.

cases.name: op_level_hlc_in_the_future_quarantines
cases.note: F15: an unbounded wall_ms would pin a field against every future edit. Beyond the skew bound the op quarantines whole.

cases.name: op_level_hlc_member_not_author_quarantines
cases.note: F15: the op-level HLC member must be the header's author, or a member could win tie-breaks under someone else's identity.

cases.name: quarantined_op_does_not_stop_the_stream
cases.note: A bad op is set aside and surfaced; the next valid op still applies.

cases.name: junction_revive_after_unassign
cases.note: A junction's entity id is the uuid5 of its pair, so re-assigning the same tag after an unassign revives the *same* entity rather than forking. The re-assertion is newer than the tombstone, so the row is live again.

cases.name: junction_unassign_is_a_tombstone_not_absence
cases.note: Unassignment tombstones the pair. A replayed assertion older than the tombstone cannot resurrect it, in either arrival order.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_stale_later_value_wins
cases.note: The snooze floor: the value join is a total order on the value alone, so the later floor survives a newer write carrying an earlier one. The clock joins independently as the HLC max, which is why it belongs to the *losing* value here.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_instant_tie_breaks_on_canonical_bytes
cases.note: Two spellings of one instant. The tie falls to the greater canonical JSON encoding, byte-wise — '"…:00Z"' beats '"…:00.000Z"' because 'Z' > '.'. Total, so associative.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_unparseable_loses_to_parseable
cases.note: Any parseable timestamp outranks any unparseable value, whatever the clocks say — the newer write here is the unparseable one and still loses the value.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_all_unparseable_orders_by_bytes
cases.note: With nothing parseable the order is the canonical byte order, which keeps the join total rather than falling back to LWW — the fallback was the non-associative part.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_clear_then_later_resnooze_revives
cases.note: Clear (a tombstone) then a re-snooze whose clock is newer: tombstone visibility still arbitrates by plain HLC, so the floor is live again.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_stale_clear_loses_to_resnooze
cases.note: A clear older than the re-snooze cannot silence it.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_clear_then_earlier_resnooze_keeps_preclear_floor
cases.note: The owned divergence from ADR-0011's pairwise matrix (ADR-0030): the value join is a max over every value ever asserted, so a re-snooze carrying an *earlier* value after a clear revives the field at the pre-clear floor. The floor never shrinks through a clear — it errs toward longer silence and never re-fires early.

cases.name: max_timestamp_value_three_op_associativity
cases.note: Mandatory associativity probe: three writes carrying a parsed-instant tie *and* an unparseable member, applied in all six orders. A pairwise vector cannot catch a non-associative join; this one can.

cases.name: set_merge_unions_concurrent_additions
cases.note: Concurrent additions on two devices both survive, sorted by canonical JSON encoding so the merged value is byte-identical everywhere rather than order-dependent.

cases.name: set_merge_three_op_associativity
cases.note: Three additions with an overlapping member, in all six orders — the same associativity requirement the timestamp join carries.

cases.name: set_merge_unsorted_first_write_is_canonical_and_replay_safe
cases.note: ADR-0030(a) idempotence on a *non-canonical* input. The first write into an empty field has nothing to union with, so it is the one path that could store a caller's array in arrival order; the third op re-asserts that same op verbatim. Both the reduced value and its clock must be unmoved by the re-assertion, because that re-assertion is precisely what a #555 compaction op does to every value it carries forward.

cases.name: strategy_selection_uses_the_carried_key
cases.note: Strategy selection reads nothing but the op. Both writes carry `key`, so `max_timestamp_value` is picked from the op alone and no stored state is consulted — which is what makes selection order-independent structurally rather than by policy (#563). The selection-layer twin of max_timestamp_value_stale_later_value_wins: same reduction, asserted for where the strategy came from.

cases.name: user_preferences_value_without_key_is_refused
cases.note: A `user_preferences` write carrying `value` must name the key that selects its strategy. The first op omits `key` and the second carries a non-string one: both are unresolvable for selection, both are refused under the same code rather than defaulted to LWW, since that default was the order-dependence (#563). The third op is well-formed and applies, so a refusal wedges neither the entity nor the stream. Not permuted — quarantine is a per-arrival fact the permutation harness cannot assert; the refused ops carry the *later* floor, so a guard that failed to fire would show up as a changed reduced value.

cases.name: compaction_snapshot_is_absorbed_by_the_originals
cases.note: The snapshot alongside the ops it supersedes, in every order. Equal HLC is an idempotent skip per field, so a device holding full history applies it as a no-op — and the permutation is what makes that absorption rather than a fact about one arrival order.

cases.name: compaction_snapshot_alone_reduces_to_the_same_state
cases.note: The fresh-device case: the snapshot with none of its originals. It produces the identical reduced state *and* the identical per-field clocks as compaction_snapshot_is_absorbed_by_the_originals, which is the whole equivalence claim — the compactor's own newer clock appears nowhere in the result.

cases.name: compaction_snapshot_loses_to_a_newer_concurrent_edit
cases.note: An offline device's later write to a compacted field wins exactly as it would have won against the original op, because the snapshot carries the original's clock and not the compactor's.

cases.name: compacted_tombstone_applies_at_its_original_clock
cases.note: tombstone_hlc is device A's older clock while field b is device B's newer one, so b stays live and the entity is not buried. Re-stamped with the compactor's op-level clock the tombstone would swallow b — a resurrection the original tombstone could never have swallowed.

cases.name: compaction_field_without_its_own_clock_is_refused
cases.note: The class-4 shape guard, at the reducer boundary this time: a field defaulting to the op-level clock would be stamped with the compactor's and win merges the op it supersedes would have lost. The well-formed op after it still applies, so a refusal wedges neither the entity nor the stream.
